第二部分：題組 (第20 - 43題，共24題) (20-21) Rex is a dog that lives at the bakery next to our school. He is cute and friendly. Every morning, he stands in front of the school to welcome everybody. We all see Rex as one of us. But one Monday morning, I was surprised that Rex was not there to say hello to us. "Rex is in the hospital. He was hit by a car last night," my classmate told me. We went to see Rex in the hospital that day after school. Two weeks later, Rex was much better, and we decided to take him for a walk every evening. Because of the exercise, Rex became healthier and stronger. Soon he could happily run and jump again. He is now as handsome and strong as before! 20. What happened to Rex? (A) He got lost. (B) He got hurt. (C) He bit people. (D) He ate too much. 21. How did the writer help Rex? (A) By calling the police. (B) By making him exercise. (C) By taking him to see a doctor. (D) By looking for a new home for him. 3

(22-23) 22. What do we know about Mark from the dialogue? (A) He made Linda unhappy. (B) He is looking for a new job. (C) He did not like Linda's cake. (D) He is getting married to Jenny. 23. Which is most likely an example of stealing someone＇s thunder?  likely 可能 (A) Dennis never changes his mind except when his wife tells him to. (B) Melisa tells Tom she'll go to the party but tells her mom she'll stay home. (C) Jeff tells everyone he'll move abroad when Ivy is still telling them about her baby. (D) Alisa says she doesn't care what we have for lunch but also doesn't like the restaurant we chose. 4 請翻頁繼續作答

(24-25) Buy a White Lake City Card When You're in the City  With any of the Cards, you can - visit the city by metro, bus, or train as many times as you want. * - take one child under 12 with you for free. - save 20% on tickets to public museums.  The 1-day, 3-day, and 5-day Cards are for trips from Monday to Friday, and the Weekend Card is for trips on weekends and holidays.  Check the map and buy the right Card for the zones you'll be entering. Card Zone 1 Zones 1-2 Zones 1-3 1-day 3-day $20 $40 $60 5-day $40 $60 $80 Weekend $50 $80 $110 * The Cards are only for trips inside the three zones. $30 $50 $80 ⓐ White Lake Main Station ⓑ Museum of White Lake City History ⓒ Museum of Modern Art ⓓ White Lake ⓔ White Lake Castle ⓕ White Lake Airport  zone 區 24. What can you do with a White Lake City Card? (A) Save 20% on children's train tickets. (B) Visit any public museum in the city for free. (C) Take a train to places out of the three zones. (D) Move around the city by metro as much as you want. 25. Stacy is going to White Lake City and is staying at a hotel near the White Lake Main Station. She wants to visit the Museum of White Lake City History on Friday and see White Lake on Saturday. If she plans to buy (a) White Lake City Card(s), which of the four choices will be best for her and cost her the least? (A) A 3-day Card for Zone 1. (B) A Weekend Card for Zones 1-3. (C) A 1-day Card for Zone 1 and a Weekend Card for Zones 1-2. (D) A 1-day Card for Zones 1-2 and a Weekend Card for Zones 1-2. 5

(26-28) At 5 o'clock every morning, while most people are sleeping, 16-year-old Libby Larson is already up. She mops the floor, gets the mail and the newspapers, and gets ready for visitors to Rolling Acres. Libby's grandparents started Rolling Acres in 1970, and since then all of the Larson family have been working there. Rolling Acres used to be just a sheep farm, but now, with its fruit trees, vegetable gardens, and many other kinds of animals, it has become a popular place for families to go on vacation. Visitors can pick fruits, collect eggs, and feed the animals. It is one of Libby's jobs to show kids how to feed the baby sheep. For her work, Libby is paid $10 an hour. This summer, she expects to make about $1,200 and plans to buy a cell phone. Her friends think it's great to make that much money in a summer. However, for Libby, working at a family business also means making sacrifices. "I'd love to sleep until noon or go to summer camp like other kids. My friends stopped inviting me on trips because I'm always busy in the summer." However, Libby also said, "But it's better to see both sides. Working with your family is great. You feel closer to each other." 26. What is Rolling Acres? (A) A zoo. (B) A campground. (C) A vacation farm. (D) A family restaurant. 27. What do we learn from the first paragraph?  paragraph 段落 (A) What Libby does at Rolling Acres. (B) What visitors think of Rolling Acres. (C) Why Libby's grandparents started Rolling Acres. (D) What the Larson family's plans are for Rolling Acres. 28. What does making sacrifices mean? (A) Learning to make money and use it wisely. (B) Getting to know different sides of your family. (C) Making excuses for failing to do something difficult. (D) Giving up something important to do something else. 6 請翻頁繼續作答

(29-31) Around the year 400, people came to Easter Island. So many trees here! In their free time, they loved They used trees to make fire and making statues with big rocks. With build houses. Because of the trees, the trees they cut down, they could people had a great life on the island. move the statues around easily. Trees were needed and used in every part of their life. Years passed, and there were fewer and fewer trees on Easter Island. Without enough trees to keep And I'm hungry. water under the ground, the land I'm thirsty. became dry, and plants didn't grow. 7

People began to fight for water and food. The statues were moved to fighting grounds to show their power. The last trees were probably cut down at this time. Let's not make Earth, our only home, Those who cut down another Easter Island. the last trees surely understood how important trees were to them—but still, they did it. When the last trees fell to the ground, people on the island fell, too. 29. What do the comics tell us? (A) Enjoy life while we can. (B) Follow the old ways of life. (C) Save our planet before it's too late. (D) Treat others the way we want to be treated. 30. What can we learn about the people in the comics? (A) They made fire before starting a fight. (B) They fought for land and plants all the time. (C) They prayed to the statues beside a large fire. (D) They used statues to show how strong they were. 31. What does did it in Picture 7 mean? (A) Fall to the ground. (B) Cut down the last trees. (C) Move the statues to fighting grounds. (D) Understand how important trees were. 8 請翻頁繼續作答

(32-34) Many years ago, Dan Ariely bought a cabinet from IKEA. IKEA is a famous furniture store that sells boxes of furniture parts. People who buy them have to put all the parts together themselves. It took Ariely hours to build his cabinet. Ariely didn't really enjoy himself when he was trying to put all the parts together. However, after he finished, he felt quite good about himself and his cabinet. Later, he found that he loved his cabinet more than any of his other furniture. Ariely wanted to know if anyone shared his feelings, so he did a fun origami study. He invited two groups of people to join his study. He called one group "builders" and the other group "buyers." Builders were told to make origami, like paper frogs or paper birds. When they finished, they were asked how much they would spend on their works. Ariely then showed the origami to buyers and asked them how much they would pay for them. The two groups gave very different answers. Though buyers would pay only five cents for builders' origami, builders would spend 25 cents! Interestingly, builders believed others would think their works were good enough to cost that much money! Ariely's study showed that he was not alone in his IKEA experience — we just love things more, sometimes blindly, when we make them ourselves. Ariely called it "the IKEA effect."  effect 效應 furniture 家具 32. What did Ariely try to find out in the origami study? (A) If he could stop the IKEA effect. (B) Why people love making origami. (C) Why IKEA furniture is so famous. (D) If anyone shared his IKEA experience. 33. Which is true about the origami study? (A) Buyers would spend less on builders' origami than builders would. (B) Builders and buyers needed to decide a price on the origami they made. (C) Builders knew others would not pay as much for the origami as they would. (D) Buyers would spend more on builders' origami after knowing how they were made. 9

  1. Jerry just can't get his daughter Mia to eat more vegetables at dinner. Every time he tries to do so, there is always a lot of shouting and crying. If Jerry wants to have Mia eat more vegetables by using the IKEA effect, what should he do? (A) Tell Mia that he cooks the vegetables just for her. (B) Ask Mia to help him cook vegetables for her meal. (C) Give Mia her favorite candy after she eats vegetables. (D) Ask Mia what vegetables she likes and cook them for her. 10 請翻頁繼續作答

(35-37) In the picture is a UK electricity worker in the 1970s. Pictures like this appeared in many newspapers at the time. In 1972, electricity workers in the UK asked to be paid more, and they decided to stop working until their wish was answered. The government worried that there wouldn't be enough electricity for the country if these workers didn't go to work, so it agreed to give them the pay rise. However, the story didn't end there. A year later, the electricity workers asked for another pay rise. To get what they wanted, they worked shorter hours and acted like they would walk away from their job anytime. But this time, the government decided to fight. To save electricity, it made new rules for people to follow. For example, each family could turn on the heat in only one room; TV stations had to stop their shows at 10:30 p.m.; businesses could open only three days a week. People's lives were greatly changed. Without enough heat to keep the house warm, people covered themselves in blankets all the time. Hospitals had to use candles because they couldn't keep all the lights on. Factories couldn't keep their machines working. Many people lost their jobs. For months, people were paying the price while the electricity workers were fighting for their wish. In the end, the government agreed to the second pay rise. This picture shows what many people thought of the electricity workers during the "dark" time.  electricity 電力 government 政府 35. What is the reading mainly about? (A) The tips on using a picture to tell a story. (B) The change that electricity brought to people's lives. (C) The history behind the picture of a UK electricity worker. (D) The story of a famous UK electricity worker from the 1970s. 11

  1. In the UK in the 1970s, what did people most likely think of the UK electricity workers? (A) They were not brave enough to fix their problems. (B) They worked like robots and never learned to change. (C) They were asking too much and did not know when to stop. (D) They did not care whether their job might hurt people's health.
  2. Why does the writer put the " " mark around the word dark in the last sentence? (A) To say that the "dark" time was actually not dark. (B) To tell people that the word was said by the government. (C) To mean both the days without lights and the difficult lives people lived. (D) To show that the government and the electricity workers both lost their fights. 12 請翻頁繼續作答

(38-43) Most kids want gifts from their parents on their birthdays, but Cameron doesn't. On his birthday, he gives his mom a gift. He 38 doing this in his first year of junior high school. That year, during one class, he watched a video about how a baby is pushed from its mother's body. After class, 39 . How brave a woman is to have a baby! Thank God I'll never have to do that! When Cameron came home that day, he held his mom in his arms for a long time. He decided that his birthday 40 . During those nine months inside his mom, he just ate and slept while his mom was doing all the hard work. So why should he get a birthday gift for doing nothing? If anyone should get a gift on his birthday, it should be his mom. The 41 "birthday gift" Cameron prepared was a bag of cookies he baked. The cookies tasted so bad, but his mom said they were the best thing she ever got. Hearing that 42 . It was so much better than getting a gift. Now, on his birthday every year, Cameron makes a gift for his mother to thank her for giving him life. This year, Cameron 43 his mom a nice dress. A few months ago, he learned to make dresses at school and decided to make one for his mom. Now the dress is finished and hanging behind Cameron's bedroom door. He believes the gift will tell his mother how much he loves her. 38. (A) starts (B) started (C) has started (D) will start 39. (A) he got quite scared of two things (B) he still couldn't understand two things (C) he couldn't stop thinking about two things (D) he did two things that would change his life 40. (A) should be spent helping his mom (B) should be a time of welcoming a new start (C) should not be about him, but about his mom (D) should not be celebrated for just one day, but for nine months 41. (A) first (B) last (C) only (D) other 42. (A) made his head hurt (B) made his heart sing (C) made him change his mind (D) made him give up baking 43. (A) is going to give (B) gives (C) has given (D) gave 13 試題結束

docs.title: 🎯 高考高頻 350 單字（GK-350）
docs.text: 資料來源：中國高考英語高頻詞彙，含 KK音標、例句與中譯 共 350 個高頻單字，按動詞、名詞等主題分類

1. adapt /əˈdæpt/

(v) 适应；改编（常考搭配：adapt to 适应；adapt sth for 为……改编） 📝 New students should adapt to the school life as soon as possible. 📖 新生应当尽快适应校园生活。

2. adopt /əˈdɒpt/

(v) 采用；采纳；收养（常考搭配：adopt a method/plan 采用方法/计划） 📝 Many schools have adopted new teaching methods in recent years. 📖 近年来许多学校都采用了新式教学方法。

3. affect /əˈfekt/

(v) 影响；使感动 📝 Stress will greatly affect students’ learning efficiency. 📖 压力会极大影响学生的学习效率。

4. afford /əˈfɔːd/

(v) 负担得起；提供（常考搭配：afford to do sth 负担得起做某事） 📝 Few people can afford such an expensive house in big cities. 📖 在大城市里，很少有人能买得起如此昂贵的房子。

5. analyze /ˈænəlaɪz/

(v) 分析 📝 We should analyze problems calmly when we meet difficulties. 📖 遇到困境时，我们应当冷静分析问题。

6. approach /əˈprəʊtʃ/

(v) 靠近；处理 n. 方法；途径（常考搭配：approach to doing sth 做某事的方法） 📝 We need a new approach to solving this difficult problem. 📖 我们需要新方法来解决这道难题。

7. assess /əˈses/

(v) 评估；评价 📝 Teachers usually assess students’ progress at the end of each term. 📖 老师通常在每学期末评估学生的学习进度。

8. assist /əˈsɪst/

(v) 帮助；协助（常考搭配：assist sb in/with sth 帮助某人做某事） 📝 Volunteers assist teachers in organizing after-school activities. 📖 志愿者协助老师开展课外活动。

9. assume /əˈsjuːm/

(v) 假定；认为；承担 📝 We cannot always assume that everything will go well. 📖 我们不能想当然地认为万事都会一帆风顺。

10. attach /əˈtætʃ/

(v) 附上；重视；依恋（常考搭配：attach importance to 重视） 📝 Nowadays, more people attach great importance to physical exercise. 📖 如今，越来越多人十分重视体育锻炼。

11. attempt /əˈtempt/

(v) &n. 尝试；努力（常考搭配：attempt to do sth 尝试做某事） 📝 He made every attempt to improve his English writing skills. 📖 他竭尽全力提升自身的英语写作能力。

12. avoid /əˈvɔɪd/

(v) 避免；避开（常考搭配：avoid doing sth 避免做某事） 📝 We should avoid making careless mistakes in the exam. 📖 考试中我们要避免犯下粗心的错误。

13. balance /ˈbæləns/

(v) 平衡 n. 平衡；余额（常考搭配：balance A and B 平衡A与B） 📝 It is important to balance study and relaxation for senior high students. 📖 高中生平衡好学习与放松至关重要。

14. benefit /ˈbenɪfɪt/

(v) 受益 n. 益处（常考搭配：benefit from 从……受益；be of benefit to 对……有益） 📝 Students can benefit a lot from reading English classics. 📖 阅读英语经典著作能让学生收获良多。

15. combine /kəmˈbaɪn/

(v) 结合；联合（常考搭配：combine A with B 将A与B结合） 📝 We should combine theory with practice in our study. 📖 学习过程中我们要做到理论结合实际。

16. concentrate /ˈkɒnsntreɪt/

(v) 集中（注意力）（常考搭配：concentrate on 专注于） 📝 You must concentrate on your studies in class. 📖 课堂上你必须专心听讲学习。

17. consume /kənˈsjuːm/

(v) 消耗；耗费；消费 📝 Playing mobile games too much consumes plenty of our spare time. 📖 过度玩手机会耗费我们大量课余时间。

18. contribute /kənˈtrɪbjuːt/

(v) 贡献；促成；导致（常考搭配：contribute to 有助于；导致） 📝 Regular exercise contributes to good health and a strong body. 📖 规律运动有助于强身健体。

19. convey /kənˈveɪ/

(v) 传达；传递（情感、信息） 📝 This article conveys the author’s love for hometown. 📖 这篇文章抒发了作者对家乡的热爱之情。

20. convince /kənˈvɪns/

(v) 说服；使确信（常考搭配：convince sb of sth 使某人确信某事） 📝 I finally convinced my parents to support my hobby. 📖 我最终说服父母支持我的爱好。

21. deserve /dɪˈzɜːv/

(v) 值得；应得 📝 Every effort you make deserves to be respected. 📖 你付出的每一份努力都值得被尊重。

22. determine /dɪˈtɜːmɪn/

(v) 决定；确定（常考搭配：determine to do sth 决心做某事） 📝 He determined to work harder to realize his dream. 📖 他下定决心加倍努力，实现自己的梦想。

23. develop /dɪˈveləp/

(v) 发展；培养；养成（常考搭配：develop a habit 养成习惯） 📝 We should develop the habit of keeping a diary every day. 📖 我们应当养成每日写日记的习惯。

24. devote /dɪˈvəʊt/

(v) 致力于；奉献（常考搭配：devote oneself to doing sth 致力于做某事） 📝 Many teachers devote all their time to educating students. 📖 许多老师倾尽心血培育学生。

25. differ /ˈdɪfə/

(v) 不同；有差异（常考搭配：differ from 与……不同） 📝 My learning method differs from my deskmate’s. 📖 我的学习方法和同桌的有所不同。

26. discard /dɪsˈkɑːd/

(v) 丢弃；抛弃 📝 We should discard bad habits and develop good ones. 📖 我们要摒弃陋习，养成良好习惯。

27. display /dɪˈspleɪ/

(v) &n. 展示；陈列 📝 Students’ excellent works are displayed on the school wall. 📖 校园墙上陈列着同学们的优秀作品。

28. distribute /dɪˈstrɪbjuːt/

(v) 分配；分发 📝 The teacher distributes learning materials to every student. 📖 老师给每位学生分发学习资料。

29. dominate /ˈdɒmɪneɪt/

(v) 主导；支配；占据 📝 Positive attitudes should dominate our daily study and life. 📖 积极的心态应当主导我们日常的学习与生活。

30. donate /dəʊˈneɪt/

(v) 捐赠；捐献（常考搭配：donate sth to sb 向某人捐赠某物） 📝 Many students donate books to children in mountain areas. 📖 不少学生向山区孩子捐赠书籍。

31. ensure /ɪnˈʃʊə/

(v) 确保；保证 📝 Careful checking can ensure no mistakes in the exam. 📖 仔细检查能够保证考试少出纰漏。

32. establish /ɪˈstæblɪʃ/

(v) 建立；创立；确立 📝 Our school established a new reading club last year. 📖 我校去年创办了新的读书社团。

33. evaluate /ɪˈvæljueɪt/

(v) 评估；评价 📝 We need to evaluate our study state every month. 📖 我们每月都要复盘评估自身的学习状态。

34. evolve /iˈvɒlv/

(v) 发展；进化；逐步演变 📝 People’s understanding of life is evolving with time. 📖 人们对生活的认知随着时间不断变化。

35. exchange /ɪkˈsteɪndʒ/

(v) &n. 交换；交流（常考搭配：exchange ideas 交流想法） 📝 We often exchange learning experience with classmates. 📖 我们常常和同学交流学习心得。

36. expand /ɪkˈspænd/

(v) 扩大；拓展；膨胀 📝 Reading can expand our horizons and enrich our minds. 📖 阅读能够拓宽眼界、丰富思想。

37. expect /ɪkˈspekt/

(v) 期待；预料（常考搭配：expect to do sth 期待做某事） 📝 We all expect to get good grades in the final exam. 📖 我们都期盼期末考试能取得优异成绩。

38. explain /ɪkˈspleɪn/

(v) 解释；说明 📝 The teacher patiently explains difficult knowledge points to us. 📖 老师耐心地为我们讲解重难点知识。

39. explore /ɪkˈsplɔː/

(v) 探索；探究 📝 Teenagers should keep curious and explore new things. 📖 青少年应保持好奇心，不断探索新鲜事物。

40. expose /ɪkˈspəʊz/

(v) 暴露；使接触（常考搭配：be exposed to 接触；暴露于） 📝 Being exposed to English every day helps improve oral English. 📖 每日接触英语有助于提升口语水平。

41. focus /ˈfəʊkəs/

(v) 聚焦 n. 焦点（常考搭配：focus on 专注于；聚焦于） 📝 We should focus on improving our comprehensive ability. 📖 我们要着力提升自身综合素养。

42. forbid /fəˈbɪd/

(v) 禁止；不许（常考搭配：forbid doing sth 禁止做某事） 📝 Schools forbid students from using phones in class. 📖 学校禁止学生课堂上使用手机。

43. generate /ˈdʒenəreɪt/

(v) 产生；引发 📝 Positive moods can generate more motivation for study. 📖 愉悦的心情能催生更多学习动力。

44. guarantee /ˌɡærənˈtiː/

(v) &n. 保证；担保 📝 Hard work cannot guarantee success, but it brings hope. 📖 努力未必能保证成功，但一定会带来希望。

263. efficient /ɪˈfɪʃnt/

(adj) 高效的 📝 Reasonable planning makes study more efficient. 📖 合理规划可以让学习变得更加高效。

264. essential /ɪˈsenʃl/

(adj) 必不可少的；核心的 📝 Persistence is essential for English long-term study. 📖 坚持是英语长期学习必不可少的要素。

265. evident /ˈevɪdənt/

(adj) 明显的；显而易见的 📝 It is evident that practice makes perfect. 📖 熟能生巧，这是显而易见的道理。

266. extreme /ɪkˈstriːm/

(adj) 极端的；极度的 📝 We need to avoid extreme attitudes towards study. 📖 我们要避免对待学习产生极端心态。

267. fair /feə/

(adj) 公平的；合理的 📝 Hard work is the fair way to get good results. 📖 努力付出是取得优异成绩的公平途径。

268. flexible /ˈfleksəbl/

(adj) 灵活的 📝 We need flexible thinking to solve difficult questions. 📖 解答难题需要具备灵活的思维方式。

269. frequent /ˈfriːkwənt/

(adj) 频繁的；常见的 📝 Frequent review reduces forgetting of knowledge. 📖 时常温习能够减少知识遗忘。

270. fundamental /ˌfʌndəˈmentl/

(adj) 根本的；基础的 📝 Words are fundamental to English learning. 📖 单词是英语学习的根基所在。

271. generous /ˈdʒenərəs/

(adj) 慷慨的；大方的 📝 Generous students are willing to share learning experience. 📖 大方豁达的学生乐于分享学习心得。

272. genuine /ˈdʒenjuɪn/

(adj) 真诚的；真实的 📝 Genuine efforts will never let you down. 📖 真心实意的付出终究不会白费。

273. guilty /ˈɡɪlti/

(adj) 内疚的；愧疚的 📝 You will feel guilty if you waste precious time. 📖 虚度宝贵时光会让人内心倍感愧疚。

274. identical /aɪˈdentɪkl/

(adj) 完全相同的 📝 No two students have identical learning states. 📖 没有两名学生的学习状态会完全一样。

275. ignorant /ˈɪɡnərənt/

(adj) 无知的；不了解的 📝 Do not remain ignorant of basic knowledge. 📖 不要对基础知识懵懂漠视。

276. initial /ɪˈnɪʃl/

(adj) 最初的；初始的 📝 Initial efforts lay the foundation for later progress. 📖 初期的付出为后续进步打下基础。

277. innocent /ˈɪnəsnt/

(adj) 天真的；单纯的 📝 Teenagers keep innocent and positive minds. 📖 青少年怀揣着纯真积极的本心。

278. instant /ˈɪnstənt/

(adj) 立刻的；即时的 📝 Instant correction stops repeated mistakes. 📖 及时订正能够避免错误反复出现。

279. intelligent /ɪnˈtelɪdʒənt/

(adj) 聪慧的；明智的 📝 Intelligent learning methods save plenty of time. 📖 巧妙的学习方法可以节省大量时间。

280. intense /ɪnˈtens/

(adj) 强烈的；紧张的 📝 We face intense study pressure in senior high school. 📖 高中阶段我们面临着不小的学习压力。

281. permanent /ˈpɜːmənənt/

(adj) 永久的；持久的 📝 Good habits bring permanent benefits to life. 📖 好习惯会给人生带来长久益处。

282. potential /pəˈtenʃl/

(adj) 潜在的 n. 潜力 📝 Every student has unlimited potential to improve. 📖 每位学生都拥有无限的提升潜力。

283. precise /prɪˈsaɪs/

(adj) 精确的；准确的 📝 Precise analysis helps find out weak points. 📖 精准分析有助于找出自身薄弱之处。

284. prominent /ˈprɒmɪnənt/

(adj) 显著的；突出的 📝 He made prominent progress in this semester. 📖 这一学期他取得了十分突出的进步。

285. qualified /ˈkwɒlɪfaɪd/

(adj) 合格的；胜任的 📝 Continuous improvement makes you a qualified learner. 📖 不断精进才能成为合格的学习者。

286. rare /reə/

(adj) 稀少的；罕见的 📝 Persistence is a rare precious quality. 📖 持之以恒是一种难得的可贵品质。

287. relevant /ˈreləvənt/

(adj) 相关的；贴切的 📝 Write relevant content in your English composition. 📖 英语写作中紧扣主题撰写相关内容。

288. reliable /rɪˈlaɪəbl/

(adj) 可靠的；可信的 📝 Accumulated experience is reliable learning guidance. 📖 积累的经验是可靠的学习指引。

289. responsible /rɪˈspɒnsəbl/

(adj) 负责的（常考搭配：be responsible for 对……负责） 📝 Everyone should be responsible for their own study. 📖 每个人都应当对自己的学业负责。

290. secure /sɪˈkjʊə/

(adj) 安稳的；稳固的 📝 Solid knowledge makes our study foundation secure. 📖 扎实的学识筑牢稳固的学习根基。

291. significant /sɪɡˈnɪfɪkənt/

(adj) 重大的；显著的 📝 Reading has significant influence on students’ growth. 📖 阅读对学生的成长有着深远影响。

292. similar /ˈsɪmɪlə/

(adj) 相似的（常考搭配：be similar to 与……相似） 📝 My study plan is similar to my friend’s plan. 📖 我的学习规划和朋友的大致相仿。

293. sincere /sɪnˈsɪə/

(adj) 真诚的；恳切的 📝 Sincere communication shortens the distance between people. 📖 真诚交流能够拉近人与人之间的距离。

294. strict /strɪkt/

(adj) 严格的（常考搭配：be strict with 对……严格要求） 📝 We ought to be strict with ourselves in study. 📖 学习中我们应当严格要求自我。

295. sufficient /səˈfɪʃnt/

(adj) 足够的；充分的 📝 Sufficient exercises master grammar knowledge well. 📖 足量练习才能熟练掌握语法知识。

296. superior /suːˈpɪəriə/

(adj) 优越的；更好的 📝 Positive mindset is superior to negative mood. 📖 积极心态远胜于消极情绪。

297. temporary /ˈtemprəri/

(adj) 暂时的；临时的 📝 Failure is only temporary in the road of growth. 📖 成长路上的失败都只是暂时的。

298. urgent /ˈɜːdʒənt/

(adj) 紧急的；迫切的 📝 It is urgent for us to make up for weak subjects. 📖 弥补薄弱学科是我们眼下迫切的任务。

299. vital /ˈvaɪtl/

(adj) 至关重要的 📝 Confidence is vital to overcoming learning difficulties. 📖 信心对于攻克学习难题至关重要。

300. vivid /ˈvɪvɪd/

(adj) 生动的；鲜活的 📝 Vivid examples enrich the content of articles. 📖 生动的事例能够丰富文章内容。

301. additionally /əˈdɪʃənəli/

(adv) 此外；另外 📝 Additionally, we need to strengthen oral English practice. 📖 除此之外，我们还要加强英语口语练习。

302. approximately /əˈprɒksɪmətli/

(adv) 大约；大概 📝 We spend approximately eight hours studying every day. 📖 我们每天大约花费八小时用于学习。

303. basically /ˈbeɪsɪkli/

(adv) 基本上；大体上 📝 Basically, hard work is the foundation of all achievements. 📖 大体而言，努力是一切收获的根基。

304. consequently /ˈkɒnsɪkwəntli/

(adv) 因此；结果 📝 He reviews knowledge daily; consequently, he makes steady progress. 📖 他每日温习知识，因此成绩稳步提升。

305. currently /ˈkʌrəntli/

(adv) 目前；当下 📝 Currently, more students pay attention to all-round development. 📖 当下，越来越多学生重视全面发展。

306. definitely /ˈdefɪnətli/

(adv) 肯定地；明确地 📝 Continuous efforts will definitely bring good results. 📖 坚持不懈的努力必定会收获佳绩。

307. eventually /ɪˈventʃuəli/

(adv) 最终；终于 📝 Stick to your goal, and you will succeed eventually. 📖 坚守目标，你终将会取得成功。

308. frequently /ˈfriːkwəntli/

(adv) 频繁地；常常 📝 We frequently sum up experience from daily study. 📖 我们时常总结日常学习中的经验。

309. generally /ˈdʒenrəli/

(adv) 通常；总的来说 📝 Generally speaking, good habits promote better grades. 📖 总的来说，好习惯有助于提升成绩。

310. gradually /ˈɡrædʒuəli/

(adv) 逐渐地 📝 Your vocabulary will gradually expand with daily accumulation. 📖 词汇量会在日积月累中慢慢增长。

311. hardly /ˈhɑːdli/

(adv) 几乎不 📝 He hardly wastes time on meaningless things. 📖 他几乎不会把时间耗费在无意义的事情上。

312. immediately /ɪˈmiːdiətli/

(adv) 立刻；马上 📝 Correct wrong answers immediately after exams. 📖 考完试后立刻订正错题。

313. increasingly /ɪnˈkriːsɪŋli/

(adv) 越来越多地 📝 English plays an increasingly important role in daily life. 📖 英语在日常生活中变得愈发重要。

314. merely /ˈmɪəli/

(adv) 仅仅；只不过 📝 Success depends not merely on luck, but on diligence. 📖 成功不只依靠运气，更源自勤奋。

315. normally /ˈnɔːməli/

(adv) 通常；正常地 📝 We normally finish daily tasks according to plans. 📖 我们通常依照计划完成每日任务。

316. obviously /ˈɒbviəsli/

(adv) 明显地 📝 Obviously, reading is an effective way to improve English. 📖 显而易见，阅读是提升英语的有效途径。

317. particularly /pəˈtɪkjələli/

(adv) 尤其；特别 📝 I particularly enjoy reading essays in spare time. 📖 我闲暇时格外喜欢阅读散文。

318. relatively /ˈrelətɪvli/

(adv) 相对地 📝 This grammar point is relatively easy to master. 📖 这个语法知识点相对更容易掌握。

319. roughly /ˈrʌfli/

(adv) 大致；粗略地 📝 We can roughly divide time into study and rest parts. 📖 我们可以把时间大致划分为学习与休息两部分。

320. significantly /sɪɡˈnɪfɪkəntli/

(adv) 显著地；大幅度地 📝 Proper methods can significantly raise learning efficiency. 📖 合适的方法能够大幅提升学习效率。

321. account for ``

(phr) 解释；占（比例） 📝 Hard work accounts for most people’s success in exams. 📖 勤奋努力是多数人考试取胜的原因。

322. be accustomed to ``

(phr) 习惯于 📝 Most students are accustomed to busy regular school life. 📖 大多数学生已经适应紧凑规律的校园生活。

323. be aware of ``

(phr) 意识到 📝 We must be aware of our shortcomings and improve ourselves. 📖 我们必须认清自身不足并不断完善自我。

324. be beneficial to ``

(phr) 对……有益 📝 Early sleep and early rising is beneficial to study efficiency. 📖 早睡早起有助于提升学习效率。

325. be bound to ``

(phr) 一定；注定 📝 You are bound to gain progress if you keep working hard. 📖 坚持努力，你必定会收获进步。

326. be concerned about ``

(phr) 担心；关注 📝 Parents are always concerned about children’s growth. 📖 父母始终牵挂关心孩子的成长。

327. be determined to ``

(phr) 下定决心做某事 📝 I am determined to get better grades this semester. 📖 我下定决心在本学期考取更优异的成绩。

328. be exposed to ``

(phr) 接触；置身于 📝 Being exposed to authentic English improves language sense. 📖 接触地道英语能够培养语感。

329. be involved in ``

(phr) 参与；投身于 📝 Many students are actively involved in school volunteer work. 📖 不少学生积极参与校内志愿活动。

330. be limited to ``

(phr) 局限于 📝 Learning should not be limited to textbook knowledge only. 📖 学习不应只局限于课本之内的知识。

331. be occupied with ``

(phr) 忙于 📝 She is occupied with reviewing lessons before examinations. 📖 考试前夕她一直忙于温习功课。

332. be responsible for ``

(phr) 对……负责 📝 Everyone is responsible for their own future and choices. 📖 每个人都要对自己的选择与未来负责。

333. be similar to ``

(phr) 与……相似 📝 This learning skill is similar to the teacher’s suggestion. 📖 这个学习技巧和老师给出的建议相近。

334. contribute to ``

(phr) 有助于；导致 📝 Positive mindset contributes to better learning results. 📖 积极的心态有助于取得更好的学习成效。

335. devote oneself to ``

(phr) 致力于 📝 Many teachers devote themselves to educating young students. 📖 许多老师全身心投入教书育人事业。

336. have access to ``

(phr) 可以使用；能够接触 📝 All students have access to rich online learning resources. 📖 全体学生都能使用丰富的线上学习资源。

337. in terms of ``

(phr) 就……而言；在……方面 📝 In terms of English study, persistence matters most. 📖 就英语学习来说，坚持最为重要。

338. make a difference ``

(phr) 产生影响；起到作用 📝 Small daily efforts will make a big difference in the end. 📖 日常点滴付出，最终会带来巨大改变。

339. pay attention to ``

(phr) 注意；重视 📝 Pay attention to details to avoid unnecessary mistakes. 📖 重视细节，规避不必要的失误。

340. play a role in ``

(phr) 在……中发挥作用 📝 Good daily habits play an important role in study growth. 📖 良好日常习惯在学业成长中发挥重要作用。

341. refer to ``

(phr) 查阅；参考；提及 📝 You can refer to notes when sorting out knowledge points. 📖 整理知识点时可以翻阅课堂笔记。

342. rely on ``

(phr) 依靠；依赖 📝 We cannot rely on others forever on the road of study. 📖 求学路上我们不能永远依赖他人。

343. take advantage of ``

(phr) 利用 📝 Take advantage of holiday time to expand knowledge scope. 📖 利用假期时间拓宽知识面。

344. keep pace with ``

(phr) 跟上；同步 📝 Keep pace with classroom teaching progress all the time. 📖 时刻跟上课堂的教学进度。

345. break away from ``

(phr) 摆脱；脱离 📝 Break away from lazy attitudes and study earnestly. 📖 摆脱懒散心态，认真踏实学习。

346. focus on ``

(phr) 专注于 📝 Focus on current tasks and do every thing well. 📖 专心做好当下的每一项学习任务。

347. deal with ``

(phr) 处理；应对 📝 Learn to deal with pressure and frustration properly. 📖 学会妥善应对压力与挫折。

348. make progress ``

(phr) 取得进步 📝 Keep accumulating and you will make steady progress. 📖 坚持积累，就能稳步取得进步。

349. take measures ``

(phr) 采取措施 📝 Take effective measures to improve weak subjects. 📖 采取有效办法补齐薄弱学科。

350. face up to ``

(phr) 勇敢面对 📝 Face up to difficulties instead of escaping from them. 📖 直面困难，不要选择逃避。
